policy: PROTOCOL.md ten-path curation keeps positive primary-metric paths in descending order. These two paths passed every gate (pinned release, documented local API, both valid controls equal to the CPython json oracle, container control, parser-source coverage and stable input-dependent AFL++ feedback) but rank below ten verified paths with more PyPI Stats last_month downloads after dirtyjson and hjson were verified. As in the original matrix (data/curation/preten/), the audits require every project directory to be a selected catalog row, so their project and AFL++ overlay directories, verify scripts, pilot tests and generated guides were removed; their full catalog rows, verification records and valid-feedback receipts are kept here and in this cell. The removed files are at the base commit below.
metric: PyPI Stats last_month downloads excluding known mirrors

catalog_row.name: python-rapidjson
catalog_row.input_api: rapidjson.load(io.BytesIO(local JSON bytes)); rapidjson.loads(bytes) and rapidjson.loads(decoded str) give the same exact tree on both controls
catalog_row.scope: JSON structure and values from a local binary stream; valid nested object and nested array controls, each equal to an exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree
catalog_row.family: Tencent RapidJSON C++ SAX Reader (vendored v1.1.0-763-g24b5e7a8) / python-rapidjson PyHandler wrapper
catalog_row.family_note: rapidjson.load wraps the stream in PyReadStreamWrapper (chunked .read() calls) and drives RapidJSON's GenericReader::Parse with python-rapidjson's own PyHandler, which builds Python objects from SAX events. This is the same Tencent RapidJSON C++ parser family as the C++ RapidJSON path (projects/json/cpp/rapidjson, release 1.1.0, which reaches the same GenericReader through Document::Parse with RapidJSON's own number conversion), at a later upstream revision; it is not an independent parser from that path. Independent of the CPython json, simplejson, Jiter, orjson/yyjson, yajl, msgspec and UltraJSON families in this cell.
catalog_row.number_and_key_scope: Not exercised beyond the controls; no malformed or edge-case probes were run. From the pinned rapidjson.cpp source: the default number_mode (NM_NAN) parses with kParseNumbersAsStringsFlag | kParseNanAndInfFlag, so RapidJSON's own strtod is bypassed and PyHandler::RawNumber converts integers with PyLong_FromString (arbitrary precision) and other numbers with CPython's PyOS_string_to_double; NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are accepted unless allow_nan=False. Duplicate object keys are inserted with PyDict_SetItem, so the last value wins. load() passes stream chunks to RapidJSON without kParseValidateEncodingFlag, so UTF-8 validity of bytes streams is not checked by the parser. The controls contain no duplicate keys (checked with the oracle's object_pairs_hook), only exactly representable floats (1.25 and 2.5e-1) and small integers.

popularity.limitation: Package-level downloads include encoder-only and schema-validation use and transitive installs; they do not measure JSON parsing directly.

verification_record.oracle: CPython json.loads (with _json C scanner) under /usr/bin/python3 -I in the same image, where rapidjson is not importable; exact type-tagged trees with float.hex values and object member order
verification_record.parser_family: Tencent RapidJSON C++ SAX Reader (vendored v1.1.0-763-g24b5e7a8) / python-rapidjson PyHandler wrapper
verification_record.coverage_caveat: Source-built clang -O0 extension; the official wheel compiles the same rapidjson.cpp and vendored RapidJSON headers into one optimised extension. Default number_mode routes numbers through RapidJSON's NumbersAsStrings path and CPython conversion, so RapidJSON's strtod is not exercised. The controls do not exercise duplicate keys, large or inexact numbers, NaN/Infinity tokens, invalid UTF-8 or malformed input.

catalog_row.name: pysimdjson
catalog_row.input_api: simdjson.Parser().parse(local JSON bytes, recursive=True); Parser().load(local path, recursive=True) gives the same exact tree on both controls
catalog_row.scope: JSON structure and values from local bytes; valid nested object and nested array controls, each equal to an exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree
catalog_row.family: simdjson 5.1.1 C++ DOM parser (vendored amalgamation, arm64 NEON kernel on linux/arm64) / pysimdjson Cython binding
catalog_row.family_note: Parser.parse calls simdjson's dom::parser (parse_into_document_unpadded) and the Cython csimdjson extension converts the DOM tape to Python dict/list/str/int/float. On linux/arm64 the build compiles the arm64 and fallback kernels and runtime dispatch selects arm64 (ARM NEON); no fallback-kernel line executed on either control. Same simdjson family as the C++ pilot path projects/json/cpp/simdjson, which pins simdjson 5.0.4; pysimdjson 8.0.0 vendors 5.1.1. Not combined with that C++ path. Independent of the CPython json, simplejson, Jiter, orjson/yyjson, yajl, msgspec and UltraJSON families in this cell. simdjson/__init__.py imports the stdlib json module only to re-export dumps/dump/JSONEncoder; stdlib decoding is disabled during the oracle comparison.
catalog_row.number_and_key_scope: Not exercised beyond the controls; no malformed or edge-case probes were run. From the pinned sources and docs: recursive=True conversion keeps the last value for duplicate object keys (the lazy Object proxy keeps every field and looks up the first); integers become Python int from simdjson's int64 or uint64 tape values, and integers beyond 64 bits raise ValueError (BIGINT_ERROR) rather than becoming arbitrary-precision ints; numbers with a fraction or exponent become binary64 floats from simdjson's own number parser; NaN and Infinity tokens are not accepted. The controls contain no duplicate keys (checked with the oracle's object_pairs_hook), only exactly representable floats (1.25 and 2.5e-1) and small integers.

popularity.limitation: Package-level downloads include transitive installs and uses other than parsing; they do not measure JSON parsing directly.

verification_record.parser_family: simdjson 5.1.1 C++ DOM parser (arm64 NEON kernel) / pysimdjson Cython binding
verification_record.coverage_caveat: Source-built Cython 3.3.1 / clang -O0 extension; the official aarch64 wheel compiles the same sources optimised. Wrapper lines are in Cython-generated csimdjson.cpp (including module initialisation), not mapped back to csimdjson.pyx. Wrapper feedback is identical on both controls; the input-dependent difference is entirely in simdjson's arm64 kernel. The controls do not exercise duplicate keys, integers beyond 64 bits, inexact numbers or malformed input.
